transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 min (approx)
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE); Marco Rivera (Redwood SE); Priya Patel (Redwood CSM); Alex Gomez (Nimbus Head of ML); Dana Lee (Engineering Manager); Samir Khan (Security Lead); Jules Park (DevOps)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focused on rollout/go-live planning: canary strategy, cutover steps, monitoring/alerts, runbooks, and outstanding security sign-offs. Agreed next steps include runbook draft from Redwood, 24h staging canary, security checklist completion, and a cutover rehearsal.

Topics:
- Canary design (traffic %, duration, metric thresholds)
- A/B vs canary tradeoffs and evaluation metrics
- Monitoring dashboards, alerts, and runbooks/rollback flows
- Compliance items: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency
- Final capacity and pricing discussion (dedicated vs hosted)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie (Redwood AE): alright everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45. Main goal today is to lock the canary and cutover plan and make sure security has what they need, um Priya will help with the runbook notes.
[00:18] Alex (Nimbus): yeah thanks, want to make sure the canary validates latency and cost - we saw a 12% p95 increase in the last test when the KV cache warmed slowly.
[00:30] Marco (Redwood SE): okay noted, that was the cold-KV issue, we have a couple mitigations: prefix caching warm-up and sticky warm nodes for the canary. For the canary we recommend starting at 1% traffic, 4 hour ramp to 5%, run 24h at steady state.
[00:48] Dana (Eng Manager): quick question - why not do A/B? We want a direct compare to our current hosted calls.
[00:56] Marco: good question. A/B works if you can route identical traffic and don't mind splitting user sessions. Canary is lower blast radius and simpler rollback; A/B gives cleaner comparison but higher risk during cutover. Given regulated users, canary is safer.
[01:20] Samir (Security): from security side we need audit logs to be immutable for 90 days and KMS-managed keys; also SSO/SAML mapping for RBAC. Who owns the KMS config?
[01:32] Sophie: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private, for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS - we'll send the integration guide. Action: Samir to send the specific KMS ARN and required IAM role.
[01:42] Samir: I'll send that, goal is sign-off before canary.
[01:50] Jules (DevOps): on cutover, what's the expected rollback time if we need to flip back?
[01:56] Marco: with the canary at 5% we expect to stop routing within 30s, full rollback depends on DNS/edge caches; we recommend a staged rollback plan: immediate traffic cut, then model variant swap, then scale down nodes. We'll include exact commands in the runbook.
[02:15] Dana: and what about metrics - what are we monitoring to decide if canary passes?
[02:20] Marco: primary: p95 latency (target < 460ms), error rate (<0.2% increase over baseline), token cost within 8% of baseline, and qualitative failure modes in the first 4 hours. We'll also track KV hit rate and memory pressure.
[02:45] Alex: can we have automated gating? like prometheus alert that auto-triggers rollback?
[02:50] Marco: yes, we can set composite alerts: if p95 > threshold AND error rate spike > X for 5 minutes trigger an alert. Auto-rollback is risky but we can automate a circuit-breaker that will stop routing new sessions to the canary.
[03:08] Sophie: note to team - balancing latency vs cost came up last call; customer asked for dedicated pricing for the final commit. I have a pricing delta to send after today's session.
[03:20] Alex: perfect. One other constraint - we need to ensure no customer PII leaves region; how does Redwood handle residency with Dedicated?
[03:30] Sophie: Dedicated supports region pinning; for Private we can do VPC+on-prem. We'll include export controls and audit link in the security doc.
[03:40] Samir: on logs, we also need access controls for redwood console - SSO groups mapping for read-only vs admin.
[03:48] Priya (CSM): we've done mappings for other enterprise customers, I'll share a template SAML mapping.
[03:55] Dana: runbook detail - include the exact steps for smoke tests post-cutover and what to validate for each critical route.
[04:05] Marco: yep, smoke tests: 1) end-to-end generation on 3 sample heavy prompts, 2) KV cache warm check, 3) latency histogram validation, 4) billing token spike sanity. We'll put commands and expected outputs.
[04:25] Sophie: let's talk timeline: proposed canary in staging 2026-07-15 for 24h, security sign-off by 2026-07-16, cutover rehearsal 2026-07-20, production cut 2026-07-22. Does that work?
[04:40] Alex: that's workable if the runbook and benchmarks are shared early.
[04:45] Jules: need at least two rehearsal runs before production.
[04:48] Sophie: ok add a rehearsal on 2026-07-19 as well.
[04:55] Samir: one more - SOC2 artifacts and penetration test report, can Redwood provide redacted copies?
[05:02] Marco: yes we'll share SOC2 cert and redacted pentest. Expect them in the security bundle.
[05:10] Dana: how will we measure A/B quality if we decide to do a side-by-side later?
[05:15] Marco: we'd capture the same prompt set and run both variants; compute rouge/semantic similarity and human evals on a sample; but for rollout we prefer canary.
[05:28] Alex: also want a dashboard for canary: p50/p95/p99, errors, kv hit, token cost, request volume, and a user-facing SLA gauge.
[05:38] Marco: SE will prepare a Grafana dashboard and a pre-built dashboard in Redwood Console we can link.
[05:45] Priya: and we'll wire PagerDuty alerts for critical thresholds.
[05:50] Sophie: pricing - I'll send the committed monthly price and delta for dedicated GPU pools for expected throughput (final numbers by tomorrow).
[05:58] Dana: FYI our legal wants to confirm data retention and deletion windows before cutover.
[06:03] Samir: we'll own legal review from our side; we'll need the retention docs from Redwood.
[06:10] Marco: action: compile retention / audit / KMS docs into a single security bundle.
[06:16] Sophie: ok, let's recap next steps and owners at the end.
[06:22] --- (brief cross talk while notes are recorded) ---
[06:50] Sophie: recap: Marco to draft runbook + Grafana dashboard, Sophie to send pricing delta and final timeline, Jules to provision staging capacity and run tests, Samir to provide KMS and security constraints, Dana to confirm on-call and legal review.
[07:10] Alex: thanks all - we'll prioritize security sign-off so the canary isn't blocked.
[07:18] Sophie: good, we'll target runbook by Monday 2026-07-12. Any final questions?
[07:25] Dana: none from me.
[07:28] Jules: all good.
[07:30] Sophie: thanks everyone, notes and action items in the calendar invite.

End of call.

References/Links mentioned:
- Redwood canary/runbook template (link to be sent)
- Security bundle: SOC2 + redacted pentest + retention docs (to be shared)
- Benchmark script and sample traces (SE to upload)
